title: Limits and the derivative

points.text: Informal idea of a limit (gradient of chords approaching the tangent)
Derivative as gradient function and as rate of change; notation

bigPicture: The derivative is the gradient of the curve at a point: the limit of chord gradients as the chord shrinks. It also measures a rate of change.

keyIdeas.cue: How is the derivative defined informally?
keyIdeas.answer: As h → 0, the gradient (f(x+h) − f(x))/h of the chord approaches the tangent gradient.
Gradient function of the curve; rate of change of y with respect to x (units y per x).

workedExamples.title: Chord to tangent
workedExamples.prompt: For f(x) = x², find the chord gradient from x = 3 to 3 + h.

misconceptions.right: It is the gradient, not the height.
dV/dt in cm³ per s, etc.

practice.prompt: For f(x) = x³, simplify the chord gradient between x = 1 and 1 + h and hence state f′(1).
V(t) is litres in a tank. The GDC gives V′(5) = −2.4. Interpret.
practice.answer: At t = 5 min the volume is falling at 2.4 L per minute

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.
